fact_checks.current_value: CNS: dizziness 22-49%, CNS: somnolence 19-28%, GI: nausea 15%, GI: vomiting 13%, neurologic: diplopia 14%, metabolic: hyponatremia 2-3%
fact_checks.proposed_value: CNS: dizziness 20-49%, CNS: somnolence 12-36%, GI: nausea 15-29%, GI: vomiting 6-36%, neurologic/eye: diplopia 10-40%, metabolic: hyponatremia 1-5% (clinically significant sodium <125 mmol/L 2.5% in controlled epilepsy studies)

fact_checks.current_value: Induces CYP3A4/UGT; inhibits CYP2C19; weaker inducer than carbamazepine; filter_enzyme_effect=Inhibitor; Weak inducer
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling supports CYP3A4/5 induction, clinically relevant CYP2C19 inhibition, and weak UGT induction; NCBI sources support weak induction and less induction than carbamazepine.

fact_checks.current_value: Precise mechanism is unknown; active MHD metabolite blocks voltage-sensitive sodium channels, stabilizes hyperexcited neural membranes, and may also increase potassium conductance and modulate high-voltage calcium channels.; mechanism_confidence=Moderate; mechanism_source_tier=FDA label
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling supports the unknown precise mechanism, primary MHD activity, voltage-sensitive sodium-channel blockade, possible potassium-conductance increase, and high-voltage calcium-channel modulation.

fact_checks.proposed_value: Sodium channel; Potassium channel; Calcium channel
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling supports voltage-sensitive sodium-channel blockade as the primary described mechanism and possible high-voltage calcium-channel modulation; it does not support alpha-2-delta binding.

fact_checks.current_value: half_life_range=Parent ~2 h; active MHD ~8-15 h; major_organ_for_metabolism=Liver cytosolic reduction/glucuronidation; renal excretion
fact_checks.proposed_value: No change, though a tighter FDA-label wording would be: Parent about 2 h; active MHD about 9 h (IR) and about 9-11 h for Oxtellar XR.
fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling supports parent half-life about 2 hours, MHD about 9 hours, hepatic cytosolic reduction/glucuronidation, and predominant renal excretion of metabolites. NCBI StatPearls supports parent 1-3.7 h and active metabolite 8-10 h.
FDA labeling states oxcarbazepine is extensively metabolized and then predominantly excreted by the kidneys; the phrase "Renal/no major metabolism" is misleading for oxcarbazepine.
